answer: Ask what a clone farm cannot buy in bulk, and the answer points at Elected imam registration with mosques council attestation. It requires a registration the council renews after mosque audits, so the anchor of scaling up is a queue of real-world chores. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The umber is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The lotus is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
